thread:
Maya - Finance: Quick follow-up from today's all‑hands on spend guardrails / procurement. Posting clarifying notes and answering the small Qs here. TL;DR: $5k p‑card threshold, PO required for >$5k, emergency exceptions handled by finance oncall. See full policy: https://redwood.internal/procurement-guidelines :point_right:

Darren - Eng: Thanks Maya — question: for Dedicated GPU commitments (multi‑month contract) do we treat that as OPEX or CAPEX for approval flow? Need to know approver chain for reserved capacity purchases.

Maya - Finance: Treat Dedicated reserved capacity like contracted services (OPEX). Approval: cost owner + eng lead + finance. For >$50k there’s an additional finance director review. If you paste the draft SOW I can fast‑track review.

Priya - Product: For hiring-related spend (e.g., agency fees or signing bonuses) — is that on the same path as vendor procurement or a separate headcount funnel?

Maya - Finance: Headcount & recruiting fees use the People Ops approval flow (submit via Workday requisition or internal hiring form). If it's a one‑off vendor (contract recruiter) then procurement path applies. Tag @Elena if you need help mapping.

Sam - Infra: Dev/test cloud bursts: temporary large spend spikes during benchmarks — can teams pre-authorize a burst window or do we file post‑hoc emergency requests?

Maya - Finance: You can request a pre-authorized burst by filling the temporary budget form and setting an expected ceiling. Use the subject line `Burst: <team> <dates>`. If unexpected, file an emergency spend ticket and ping finance oncall — include spike metrics.

Elena - People Ops: Small one — employee travel + conference fees: p‑card ok up to $2k/person?

Maya - Finance: Yes p‑card ok up to $2k for travel with receipts and policy checklist. Above that, pre‑approval required and cost owner + manager signoff.

procure-bot: Reminder — when submitting procurement requests, attach vendor quote and SOW. Missing docs delay approval.

Darren - Eng: One last practical ask: can we get a short cheat sheet with the common paths (p‑card, PO, reserved capacity, emergency)? Some teams still unsure which form to use.

Maya - Finance: Yup — working on a one‑pager. ETA EOD Friday. For now use the quick matrix:
```
< $5k -> p-card
$5k - $50k -> PO via procurement form
> $50k -> PO + finance director review
Dedicated capacity -> contract route, OPEX approvals
Emergency -> finance oncall (submit emergency ticket)
```

Maya - Finance: Action items: 1) I'll share the one‑pager Friday. 2) @Darren pls DM the SOW if you want expedited review. 3) Teams doing benchmark bursts, create a temporary budget form before the run.

Priya - Product: Awesome, thanks. Can you also include which cost center codes to use for beta experiments?

Maya - Finance: Use `CC-PLAT-2026` for platform/prod experimentation, `CC-RD-2026` for R&D/feature experiments. I'll add that to the sheet.

Sam - Infra: Thanks all — will route the Dedicated draft to Maya this afternoon. :thumbsup:

Maya - Finance: Great — if anything urgent after hours DM me or open an emergency spend ticket and tag `#finance-oncall`. Closing the thread here but will post the one‑pager in #docs when ready. :white_check_mark:
